main_text.p: ƀunde multa dixerunt & scripserunt Ior-nandes Episcopus Rauennas, Isidorus, Pro-copius, & alii; qui ex recognitione & cum Notis Bon. Vulcanii nuper in lucem prodie-runt, quem, si placet, adi & audi.
Oratio Dominica in lingua Gothica ita habet:

p.i: Atta unsar, thu in Himma. Weihnai namo thein. Vimai thiadinassus theins, Wairthai wil-ga theins, sue ƒ in Himma, gah ana airthai. Hlaif unserana thana sintenan gif ƒns bimma daga. Gah aflet ƒns thatei sculans bi gaimasua sue gah weis afletam thaim sculam unsaraim. Gah nibriggis uns in fraeslubngai, ak lausei ƒns af thamma ubilin. Vnte theina ist thiungardi, gah mahs, gah wulthus in aiwins, Amen.

main_text.p: Hic Atta Gothis est pater, ut stte, vel stti plebi Helvetiorum: unsar noster ab Germa-nis discrepat nonnihi litera e: & Himina cœ-lum non nisi l. Quod Germanis est w hi sanctis-ficetur, id Gothis est weyhnai, ab eodem fon-te weyhen vel weyhen: vimai a veniendo La-tinorum videtur ortum, nisi malis, Latinum ortum a Gothico: & thiadinassus cum Græco ἁγιάζω affinitate habet: Wairthai fiat Ger-manis est werde: Wilga willo: sue so: gah enti vel vnti, quod cum ac Latinorum sere con-gruit prosthesi litteræ, g & aphæresi c, ip-sis & priscis Germanis trita: ana idem quod

page.notes: Printed page with a faint scan. Doubtful readings: the Gothic line "Vnte theina ist thiungardi" and some characters in the Gothic lines are uncertain; the Greek word "ἁγιάζω" is a best reading of a small printed Greek word. The "ƒ" forms in the Gothic and Latin lines are the printer's long-s and f-like forms; they may be misreadings of s, and the italic Gothic passage is transcribed as printed as far as legible. The bottom line "quod" runs into the signature area. No marginal notes are printed on this page.
